judgments.comparative_verdict: Both reports fully satisfy all four expectations with essentially equivalent grounding and citations; Report 2 adds a few extra considerations (malformed values, execution-path caveats) but this doesn't affect expectation coverage — the two are comparable in quality.

report_1.evidence: The deciding code is the function `auto_send_reminders_enabled` in `backend/app/feature_flags.py`: line 11 checks `if tenant.settings.get("auto_send_reminders") is None:` and line 12 — the exact line that decides this case — is `return True`.

report_2.evidence: The deciding code is `auto_send_reminders_enabled` in `slotwise/backend/app/feature_flags.py:10-13`. ... the check at `feature_flags.py:11` (`if tenant.settings.get("auto_send_reminders") is None:`) is true and **line 12 (`return True`) decides it**.

report_1.evidence: I would change `backend/app/feature_flags.py:12` from `return True` to `return False` (equivalently, collapse lines 11–13 to `return bool(tenant.settings.get("auto_send_reminders"))`, since `bool(None)` is `False`).

report_2.evidence: I would change `feature_flags.py:12` from `return True` to `return False` (equivalently, collapse the function to `return bool(tenant.settings.get("auto_send_reminders", False))`), making missing/None/malformed all mean off

report_1.evidence: Commit `25509a7` ("SLOT-190 tenant settings and calendar view preference", 2026-06-10) created `feature_flags.py` with one function, `compact_calendar_view_enabled`, using the `if ... is None: return True` shape... Commit `aa4cf8d`... then added `auto_send_reminders_enabled` as a structurally identical, line-for-line copy of the function directly above it... It was not a sound basis because the copied precedent and the new flag have opposite risk profiles: defaulting a display preference on affects only pixels, while defaulting auto-messaging on silently opts every existing tenant into sending SMS/email to patients.

report_2.evidence: `feature_flags.py` was created in commit `25509a7`... containing only `compact_calendar_view_enabled`, whose default-on was a deliberate, test-pinned choice for a UI preference... Commit `aa4cf8d`... then appended `auto_send_reminders_enabled` directly beneath it as a line-for-line structural copy... That basis was unsound because the two flags sit in opposite risk categories — a cosmetic view preference versus an automated outbound action toward patients

report_1.evidence: Add a global kill switch. The grep confirmed the per-tenant flag at `reminders.py:25` is the *only* gate — there is no environment-level or ops-level way to stop all sends quickly if the job misbehaves (`infra/main.tf` contains only an `environment` variable). An env-var or config check in `run()` before the tenant loop is the minimum.

report_2.evidence: Add an environment-level master switch ANDed with the per-tenant value (in the resolver or in `run()` at `reminders.py:22-25`), defaulting off, wired through deploy config. Grep shows the backend reads no environment variables at all and `infra/main.tf` contains only an `environment` variable — there is currently **no kill switch**: disabling the feature fleet-wide would require editing every tenant's settings row.
